heading: CHAPTER XV.
title: CONCERNING THINGS FOR WHICH MEN, AND ESPECIALLY PRINCES, ARE PRAISED OR BLAMED
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 15 announces Machiavelli's turn from imagined ideal polities to the real truth of political conduct.
The chapter does not yet settle a specific virtue question. It establishes the necessity test by which later chapters will judge praised and blamed qualities.
Its closing rule is stark: some seeming virtues ruin a ruler, while some seeming vices preserve security and prosperity.
